findings.summary: Node executed before its dependency gate: review-product-coherence is provisional with required artifact reviews/product-coherence.md ABSENT (no reviews/ dir in worktree), and milestone-integration (its dependency) is also provisional. The node's own constraint "Runs only after review-product-coherence corrects the product" (audit-methodology-compliance.yaml) and the deliberate ordering declared in review-product-coherence.yaml ("Runs BEFORE audit-methodology-compliance; this ordering is deliberate") were violated at dispatch. The artifact itself documents this as finding G1. The terminal audit of the graph fired while the entire upstream chain (tui-inventory, tui-methodology-audit, design-review, milestone-integration, review-product-coherence) was unresolved.

The node's chartered purpose — evidencing the graph's claims against the finished, reviewed-and-corrected product — is unfulfilled: product code is unchanged since design-review (git diff b12fde4..HEAD -- hub-rs/src lib bin/aa is empty), all design-review must/should-fix findings (F1-F18) are still live, and no Phase-2 node was implemented. The artifact is an honest baseline audit of the pre-review state, explicitly not the final gate the node's why promises ("never audits a product the reviewer just flagged"). Accepting it as the completed terminal gate would let the graph conclude with an audit of an unreviewed, uncorrected product.

Minor evidence-citation drift in the artifact: the 'all toasts = warn()' claim cites visual.rs:229-231, but toast() is defined at visual.rs:205 (229-231 is glyph_style_for); the underlying claim is true (toast() returns warn(), used at mod.rs:73-74). Should be corrected if the audit is retained.

integrity.reasoning: The artifact (audits/methodology-compliance.md) is a high-quality, scrupulously honest compliance audit: it re-checks the design-review invariants (I1-I5) and re-runs the per-surface methodology (S1-S10) with file:line citations I verified as accurate, records passes and fails, routes each violation, and refuses to fabricate a 'finished, reviewed-and-corrected' claim. The executor did the right thing under a broken dispatch. But my job is whether the node's role and the graph's integrity were preserved, and they were not. The evidence contradicts the node's stated intent and constraints from three independent sources: (1) the gddp-config mirror shows audit-methodology-compliance is the ONLY 'ready' node — all five upstream nodes are provisional; (2) the direct dependency's required artifact reviews/product-coherence.md does not exist; (3) the artifact's own G1/G2/G3 findings confirm the gate never happened and the product was never reviewed or corrected. The node's why states it 'runs only after the product review has corrected what it found, so it never audits a product the reviewer just flagged' — this audit audited exactly the product design-review flagged, with every finding still live. The graph's deliberate ordering (milestone-integration → review-product-coherence → audit) was broken at execution. There are no downstream dependents (unlocks is empty), so no dependent node is at risk, but accepting this as the terminal gate would falsely mark the graph's final gate complete. A human must decide: complete review-product-coherence (and milestone-integration) and re-run the audit, or explicitly accept this as a baseline audit of the current state. This is a sequencing/integrity failure, not a criticism of the audit document's quality or honesty.
